subject: Mock Tests
description: Official Domain Knowledge Mock Test (Paper-II Systems) covering Digital Logic, Computer Organization, Programming & DS, Algorithms, Theory of Computation, Compiler Design, Operating Systems, DBMS, and Computer Networks.

questions.question: Which of the following CPU registers is used to interface with the main memory data bus?
questions.explanation: The Memory Buffer Register (MBR) / Memory Data Register (MDR) interfaces directly with the data bus to hold data read from or written to memory.
questions.examTrick: Address Bus = MAR, Data Bus = MBR/MDR.

questions.question: The technique of executing multiple instructions in parallel by fetching them during different clock intervals is known as:
questions.explanation: Pipelining allows overlapping execution of multiple instructions during different stages of the clock cycle.
questions.examTrick: Overlapping execution stages = Pipelining.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Lexical Analyzer in a compiler?
questions.explanation: Lexical analysis (scanning) reads the input characters and groups them into meaningful sequences called tokens.
questions.examTrick: Lexical = Tokens. Syntax = Parsing / Parse Tree.

questions.question: Which data structure is used by the operating system to manage function calls and local variables?
questions.explanation: The run-time stack stores activation records (stack frames) holding local variables and return addresses for active function calls.
questions.examTrick: Function calls = Recursion / Stack (LIFO sequence).

questions.question: Which of the following sorting algorithms has a stable O(N log N) worst-case time complexity?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort is stable and guarantees O(N log N) time complexity in the worst, average, and best cases.
questions.examTrick: Quick Sort is unstable and O(N^2) worst case. Merge Sort is always O(N log N) and stable.

questions.question: In the relational model, which of the following is a candidate key?
questions.explanation: A candidate key is a minimal superkey; a set of attributes that uniquely identifies tuples and has no proper subset that does.
questions.examTrick: Candidate Key = Minimal Superkey.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model handles end-to-end connection establishment, flow control, and error recovery?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer is responsible for reliable end-to-end communication, flow control, congestion control, and error correction (using TCP).
questions.examTrick: End-to-end = Transport. Hop-by-hop = Data Link. Node-by-node / routing = Network.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height H (where root is at height 1)?
questions.explanation: The maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height H is 2^0 + 2^1 + ... + 2^(H-1) = 2^H - 1.
questions.examTrick: Height H = 2: Max nodes = 3. Plug H=2 in options: 2^2 - 1 = 3.

questions.question: In standard SQL, which clause is used to filter groups formed by the GROUP BY clause?
questions.explanation: The HAVING clause is specifically used to filter groups of rows, whereas the WHERE clause filters individual rows before grouping.
questions.examTrick: Filter rows = WHERE. Filter groups = HAVING.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-preemptive CPU scheduling algorithm?
questions.explanation: FCFS is strictly non-preemptive; once a process gets CPU, it runs to completion or until it blocks.
questions.examTrick: FCFS is always non-preemptive.

questions.question: Which memory management scheme eliminates external fragmentation completely?
questions.explanation: Paging divides physical memory into fixed-size frames, which eliminates external fragmentation because any free frame can be allocated.
questions.examTrick: Paging = No external fragmentation (only internal in the last page).

questions.question: Which of the following represents the class of languages recognized by a Pushdown Automaton?
questions.explanation: A Pushdown Automaton (PDA) is equivalent in power to a Context-Free Grammar, recognizing Context-Free Languages (CFLs).
questions.examTrick: PDA = CFL. Finite Automaton = Regular. LBA = CSL. Turing Machine = RE.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to map an IP address to its corresponding physical MAC address?
questions.explanation: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) dynamically resolves an IPv4 address to its physical hardware address (MAC).
questions.examTrick: IP to MAC = ARP. MAC to IP = RARP.

questions.question: In DBMS, the ACID property 'Durability' refers to:
options: Ensuring committed transaction modifications persist in the event of system failure.
Transactions executing in isolation from one another.
Maintaining database consistency before and after transaction.
questions.answer: Ensuring committed transaction modifications persist in the event of system failure.
questions.explanation: Durability guarantees that once a transaction commits, its updates are recorded in non-volatile storage and survive any subsequent power loss or crash.
questions.examTrick: Durability = Persistency / Survivability.

questions.question: What is the time complexity to insert an element into an AVL tree of N nodes in the worst case?
questions.explanation: Because an AVL tree is strictly balanced, searching for insertion spot and performing rotations takes O(log N) time.
questions.examTrick: AVL Tree operations are always O(log N) because height is strictly bounded by log N.

questions.question: Which of the following parser types is a Top-Down parser?
questions.explanation: Recursive Descent Parsers build parse trees from the top down by executing recursive procedures matching grammar rules. LR, SLR, and LALR are bottom-up.
questions.examTrick: LL and Recursive Descent = Top-Down. LR family = Bottom-Up.

questions.question: How many columns are there in a standard Karnaugh Map (K-map) for 4 variables?
questions.explanation: A 4-variable K-map has a 4x4 grid, meaning it has 4 rows and 4 columns, totaling 16 cells.
questions.examTrick: 4 variables = 2 variables for row (4 rows), 2 variables for col (4 columns). Grid is 4x4.

questions.question: In Unix, which system call is used to create a new child process?
questions.explanation: The fork() system call creates a new, duplicate child process that runs concurrently with the parent.
questions.examTrick: fork = duplicate child process. exec = overlay/load new program.

questions.question: What is the primary transport protocol used by Domain Name System (DNS) for query resolution?
questions.explanation: DNS query-response messages are small and fast, primarily utilizing UDP on port 53 for speed and minimal overhead.
questions.examTrick: DNS query = UDP. DNS zone transfer = TCP.

questions.question: In SQL, what is the default sorting order of the ORDER BY clause?
questions.explanation: By default, the ORDER BY clause sorts values in ascending (ASC) order unless DESC is explicitly specified.
questions.examTrick: Default is ascending.

questions.question: How many distinct states are present in an n-bit Johnson Counter?
questions.explanation: A Johnson counter (or twisted ring counter) of n bits has 2n states. It is constructed by feeding back the inverted output of the last flip-flop to the input of the first flip-flop.
questions.examTrick: Twisted counter means twisted states: n bits = 2n states. Regular Ring Counter is just n states. Easy mark!

questions.question: In standard compiler operator precedence parsing, which grammar symbol possesses the highest precedence among the following options?
questions.explanation: Identifiers (id) represent operands and have the highest precedence in operator precedence relations so that they are grouped and reduced first before operators like + and *.
questions.examTrick: Operands (id) always outrank operators. They sit at the very top of the expression evaluation hierarchy!

questions.question: What is the binary representation of the decimal fraction 0.625?
questions.explanation:
0.625 * 2 = 1.250 (Integer 1)
0.250 * 2 = 0.500 (Integer 0)
0.500 * 2 = 1.000 (Integer 1)
Reading top-down, the binary value is 0.101.
questions.examTrick: 0.625 = 0.5 (which is 1/2 = 2^-1) + 0.125 (which is 1/8 = 2^-3). This corresponds to positions 1st and 3rd after binary point: 0.101.

questions.question: Which mechanism is utilized for flow control at the Transport Layer in the TCP protocol suite?
questions.explanation: TCP uses a variable-size sliding window mechanism (Advertised Window) to achieve flow control, ensuring the sender does not overwhelm the receiver's buffer capacity.
questions.examTrick: TCP flow control is synonymous with Sliding Window (specifically dynamic window sizing based on receiver feedback).

questions.question: Consider a page reference string: 1, 2, 3, 1, 4. If the system uses the Least Recently Used (LRU) page replacement policy with 3 physical page frames (initially empty), how many page faults will occur?
questions.explanation:
Frames allocation:
- Ref 1: Fault -> [1, _, _]
- Ref 2: Fault -> [1, 2, _]
- Ref 3: Fault -> [1, 2, 3]
- Ref 1: Hit -> [1, 2, 3] (1 is now most recently used)
- Ref 4: Fault -> [1, 4, 3] (replaces least recently used 2) -> Total 4 faults.
questions.examTrick: Write down the frames and mark usage order. 1 is hit so 2 becomes the coldest, replaced by 4. Simple tracking!

questions.question: What is the equivalent postfix notation for the infix expression: A + B * C - D?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step conversion:
1. B * C -> B C *
2. A + (B C *) -> A B C * +
3. (A B C * +) - D -> A B C * + D -
questions.examTrick: Follow operator precedence. Multiplication '*' is executed first, then addition '+', then subtraction '-'. Match operators order left-to-right.

questions.question: Which of the following Unix/Linux commands is primarily used to continuously monitor active system processes and resource utilization in real-time?
questions.explanation: The 'top' command provides a dynamic, real-time view of active running processes, CPU load, and memory usage in Unix-like systems.
questions.examTrick: ps is a static snapshot, while 'top' sits at the TOP of real-time monitoring utilities.

questions.question: In a B+ tree index, if a leaf node contains keys [10, 20] and its sibling pointer P2 points to the next leaf node, which range of keys can be fetched efficiently during a range search?
questions.explanation: B+ trees store all records/pointers in leaf nodes. Sibling pointers connect leaf nodes sequentially, facilitating highly efficient range searches for keys within that leaf or across adjacent nodes (such as keys from 10 to 20).
questions.examTrick: Leaf node sequential links are specifically designed to speed up Range Queries!

questions.question: Which SQL clause corresponds directly to the Projection (pi) operator in relational algebra?
questions.explanation: The projection operator (pi) in relational algebra selects specific attributes/columns from a relation, which corresponds to the SELECT clause in SQL.
questions.examTrick: Projection is column-selection = SELECT. Selection (sigma) is row-filtering = WHERE. Do not mix them up!

questions.question: A multiplexer can be effectively used to implement which type of logic circuits?
questions.explanation: Multiplexers (MUX) are universal combinational blocks that can implement any Boolean function (combinational logic). By adding feedback (e.g., connecting outputs back to inputs), they can also implement latch/register states (sequential logic).
questions.examTrick: MUX are complete logic blocks. With feedback they can form latches/flip-flops, meaning they can do absolutely everything!

questions.question: Which level of the standard memory hierarchy possesses the longest access time but the highest capacity?
questions.explanation: Secondary Storage (like HDD/SSD) resides at the bottom of the memory hierarchy, offering maximum capacity but orders of magnitude slower access speed than CPU registers or cache.
questions.examTrick: Distance from CPU = capacity increases, speed decreases. Secondary storage is farthest from the CPU.

questions.question: A full binary tree with N leaf nodes contains how many total nodes?
questions.explanation: In any strictly full binary tree, a tree with N leaf nodes always has exactly N - 1 internal nodes, leading to a total of N + (N - 1) = 2N - 1 nodes.
questions.examTrick: Try N = 2 leaves: we have 1 root and 2 children, total = 3. Plug N=2 in options: 2(2) - 1 = 3. Quick and foolproof!

questions.question: Which of the following hashing collision resolution techniques suffers from the phenomenon of primary clustering?
questions.explanation: Linear Probing searches for the next immediate empty slot. This creates long contiguous runs of occupied slots (clusters), which increases lookup time.
questions.examTrick: Linear = contiguous line. Line-by-line probing directly builds primary clusters.

questions.question: Context-Free Languages (CFL) are NOT closed under which of the following operations?
questions.explanation: CFLs are closed under Union, Concatenation, and Kleene closure, but are NOT closed under Intersection or Complementation.
questions.examTrick: CFLs hate intersections and complements. Remember 'IC' (Intersection, Complementation) as the exceptions!

questions.question: Which compiler code optimization technique involves replacing a highly expensive operation (like multiplication) with a cheaper one (like addition)?
questions.explanation: Strength Reduction targets replacing mathematically heavy operators (e.g., x * 2) with equivalent lighter ones (e.g., x + x or x << 1).
questions.examTrick: Replacing 'heavy strength' multiplication with 'lighter' addition is literally 'Strength Reduction'.

questions.question: During a Direct Memory Access (DMA) transfer, which entity assumes control over the system's address and data buses?
questions.explanation: During active DMA transfer, the CPU relinquishes control, and the DMA Controller manages buses to complete direct High-Speed memory-device transfer.
questions.examTrick: DMA means CPU is bypassed. Controller is the boss of the bus.

questions.question: Which of the following routing protocols is classified as a Link-State Routing protocol?
questions.explanation: OSPF is a link-state protocol based on Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm, where routers build a global topology map of the network.
questions.examTrick: OSPF is Link-State (map-based), RIP is Distance-Vector (hop-count-based).

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity to find the maximum element in a min-heap containing N elements?
questions.explanation: In a min-heap, the maximum element can only reside in one of the leaf nodes. Since there are ceil(N/2) leaves, finding the maximum requires a linear scan of all leaf nodes, taking O(N) time.
questions.examTrick: Min-heap keeps minimum at root. Maximum is unsorted at the bottom leaf layer, requiring a linear O(N) search.

questions.question: Which SQL transaction isolation level prevents dirty reads but allows non-repeatable reads to occur?
questions.explanation: Read Committed ensures that a transaction can only read data that has already been committed, which prevents dirty reads, though subsequent reads of the same record might differ if another transaction commits updates.
questions.examTrick: Read Committed = only committed reads allowed. Dirty reads are blocked, but repeat reads can change.

questions.question: Which AVL tree rotation is required to restore height balance when a node becomes unbalanced due to insertion in the left subtree of its left child?
questions.explanation: Insertion in the left child's left subtree causes a Left-Left heavy imbalance, which is resolved with a single Right Rotation.
questions.examTrick: Left-Left imbalance -> Rotate Right. Double-L needs Single-R.

questions.question: Using Boolean algebraic properties, simplify the expression: F = A(A + B) + B(A' + B).
questions.explanation: A(A+B) = A (by absorption). B(A'+B) = BA' + B = B (by absorption). Thus, F = A + B.
questions.examTrick: Absorption law says A(A+B) = A. Try substituting values: A=1, B=0 gives 1; A=0, B=1 gives 1. Thus it behaves as A + B.

questions.question: What process state transition occurs when the operating system's CPU scheduler preempts a running process to allocate CPU to another thread?
questions.explanation: Preemption occurs due to interrupt/time-slice expiration. The process moves from the Running state back to the Ready queue.
questions.examTrick: Preemption does not mean blocked/waiting. The process is healthy, just waiting for its turn again, so Running -> Ready.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding Reduced Instruction Set Computer (RISC) architectures is FALSE?
options: RISC architectures have a large set of addressing modes.
Instructions are typically of fixed size.
Most instructions execute in a single clock cycle.
questions.answer: RISC architectures have a large set of addressing modes.
questions.explanation: RISC architectures are characterized by simple instruction formats and very few addressing modes. Complex Instruction Set Computer (CISC) has a large set of addressing modes.
questions.examTrick: RISC means REDUCED complexity. A large set of addressing modes is a CISC feature.

questions.question: A memory unit has a capacity of 1K x 8 bits. How many address lines and data lines are required for this memory unit?
questions.explanation: 1K = 1024 words = 2^10 words, requiring 10 address lines. Word size is 8 bits, requiring 8 data lines.
questions.examTrick: Kilo = 2^10. The exponent is the address line count. Bit width is the data line count.

questions.question: In a Pushdown Automaton, what type of stack operation is represented by the transition label 'a, Z0 / X Z0'?
questions.explanation: The label 'a, Z0 / X Z0' means upon reading input 'a' and finding stack top Z0, replace Z0 with X Z0, effectively pushing X on top of Z0.
questions.examTrick: The right side 'X Z0' has more symbols than the left side 'Z0'. This indicates symbols are being added (Push!).

questions.question: Which abstract machine model corresponds directly to Unrestricted Grammars (Chomsky Type 0)?
questions.explanation: Type 0 Grammars (Unrestricted) are recognized by Turing Machines, which have a read/write infinite storage tape.
questions.examTrick: Turing Machine is the ultimate unrestricted system. Matches Type 0 completely.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Turing machines is mathematically TRUE?
options: They can recognize any context-sensitive language.
They have a finite tape memory.
They are equivalent in power to finite automata.
questions.answer: They can recognize any context-sensitive language.
questions.explanation: Turing machines sit at the top of the Chomsky hierarchy and can recognize any context-sensitive language (since CSL is a subset of Recursively Enumerable languages).
questions.examTrick: Turing Machines are the most powerful machines and easily recognize all lower classes like CSL, CFL, and Regular.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity to search for an item in a Hash Table of size N implemented using Chaining for collision resolution?
questions.explanation: If all N keys hash to the same bucket (worst-case), the hash table collapses into a single linked list of size N, requiring O(N) search time.
questions.examTrick: Average case is always O(1) for hashing, but worst case is O(N) when a single bucket takes all hits.

questions.question: Which bus signal is asserted by the CPU to authorize the DMA controller to assume mastership of the system buses?
questions.explanation: The DMA controller asserts Bus Request (BR). Once the CPU completes its current cycle, it asserts Bus Grant (BG) to hand over control.
questions.examTrick: CPU GRANTS permission via Bus Grant (BG) after receiving a Request (BR).

questions.question: How many input bits are processed by a standard binary Full Subtractor digital circuit?
questions.explanation: A Full Subtractor processes three inputs: Minuend (A), Subtrahend (B), and Borrow-In (Bin) from the previous stage.
questions.examTrick: Subtractors are like Adders: Half subtracts 2, Full subtracts 3 inputs. Easy to remember!

questions.question: A relation R has attributes (A, B, C, D) and functional dependencies {A -> B, B -> C}. What is the highest normal form of this relation?
questions.explanation: The candidate key is AD. Attribute C depends on B, which depends on A (transitive dependency). Attribute B depends on a part of the key (A -> B), which is a partial dependency. Hence, it is not in 2NF, wait, actually since A is a proper subset of candidate key AD, and B is non-prime, A -> B is a partial dependency. Hence, the highest normal form is 1NF.
questions.examTrick: Follow standard CIL MT/GATE textbook guidelines for swift answering.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the Banker's Algorithm in modern operating systems?
questions.explanation: The Banker's Algorithm is a classic deadlock avoidance method that dynamically tests for safe states before allocating resources.
questions.examTrick: Follow standard CIL MT/GATE textbook guidelines for swift answering.

questions.question: An IP address of 192.168.1.55 with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.240 belongs to which subnet?
questions.explanation: With a mask of 255.255.255.240, subnet size is 16. Subnet intervals are multiples of 16. 16 * 3 = 48. The range is 192.168.1.48 to 192.168.1.63. 55 lies in this range, so subnet is 192.168.1.48.
questions.examTrick: Follow standard CIL MT/GATE textbook guidelines for swift answering.

questions.question: In a compiler, intermediate code generation is crucial because it:
options: Separates front-end analysis from back-end code generation.
Converts code directly to machine language.
questions.answer: Separates front-end analysis from back-end code generation.
questions.explanation: Intermediate code generation provides a machine-independent representation, isolating compiler front-ends from machine-dependent back-ends.
questions.examTrick: Follow standard CIL MT/GATE textbook guidelines for swift answering.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a process and a thread?
options: Threads share the process memory space, while processes have separate spaces.
Processes have their own stacks, while threads do not.
Threads cannot be scheduled by the CPU.
questions.answer: Threads share the process memory space, while processes have separate spaces.
questions.explanation: Threads of the same process share code, data, and OS resources, but each thread has its own private registers and stack space.
questions.examTrick: Follow standard CIL MT/GATE textbook guidelines for swift answering.

questions.question: Which of the following memory allocation algorithms suffers from external fragmentation?
questions.explanation: Segmentation allocates variable-size blocks of memory, which results in external fragmentation as chunks of memory are dynamically freed and reallocated.

questions.question: Which of the following data structures is most suitable for implementing a Priority Queue?
questions.explanation: A Binary Heap implements priority queues efficiently, providing O(log N) insertions and O(log N) deletions of the highest-priority element.

questions.question: Which of the following is an NP-Complete problem?
questions.explanation: The Travelling Salesperson Problem (TSP) is a classic NP-complete decision problem (NP-hard in optimization form) with no known polynomial-time solution.

questions.question: Which of the following database recovery protocols guarantees that no cascading rollbacks will occur?
questions.explanation: Strict 2PL requires that all exclusive locks held by a transaction be released only after the transaction commits, ensuring strict execution and preventing cascading rollbacks.

questions.question: In standard IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point format, how many bits are allocated for the exponent?
questions.explanation: IEEE 754 Single Precision (32-bit) allocates 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits, and 23 fraction/mantissa bits.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of the Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest path algorithm?
questions.explanation: Floyd-Warshall uses dynamic programming with three nested loops iterating over vertices, resulting in a time complexity of O(V^3).

questions.question: Which MAC layer protocol is used in wireless networks (802.11) to avoid packet collisions?

questions.question: The Halting Problem of Turing Machines is classified as:
questions.explanation: The Halting Problem is undecidable (no algorithm can solve it), but it is recursively enumerable (semidecidable) because a Turing machine can halt if the input halts.

questions.question: Which of the following database normal forms is strictly stronger than 3NF and handles multi-valued dependencies?

questions.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithm can lead to the convoy effect?
questions.explanation: Convoy effect occurs when a heavyweight, CPU-bound process runs first, causing all subsequent shorter I/O-bound processes to block behind it in the ready queue.
